agent.name: prov:Agent
agent.paraphrase: Something bearing responsibility for an activity, entity or another agent’s activity.

entity.name: prov:Entity
entity.paraphrase: A thing considered through fixed aspects, including conceptual or imaginary things.

association.name: prov:Association
association.paraphrase: An agent’s responsibility and role in an activity, optionally qualified by a plan.

role.name: prov:Role
role.paraphrase: A function in an activity-qualified provenance context.

person.name: prov:Person
person.paraphrase: A person considered as a provenance agent.

org.name: prov:Organization

concepts.title: Agent
concepts.authored_definition: An entity capable of performing or being accountable for relevant actions, including persons and organizations within the declared profile.
concepts.rationale: Retain the provenance-agent comparison without equating capabilities, accountability or identity policies. The Riskium Agent category aggregates bearers rather than supplying a new identity principle.
concepts.context_interpretation: The explicit AgentKinds set distinguishes human Person from Organization and remains incomplete. Excluding GS-RKM-C047 prevents bearer-kind classification from competing with responsible/authorizing participation. Changed Person/Organization typing rationales are checked at the generalization endpoints.
concepts.review_method: Assistant-supported selected-source comparison, ancestry/neighbor/set-policy review and bounded static identity/dependency checks; no instance-level or independent expert evaluation.

concepts.title: Actor Reference
concepts.authored_definition: A source-level identifier or description referring to an actor whose identity may be unresolved.
concepts.rationale: Retain the documentary-reference/agent contrast. An actor identifier or description may remain unresolved and is not itself an identified responsible or authorizing agent.
concepts.context_interpretation: G-05 inherits InformationArtifact identity; R-53 permits no resolved agent (0..1). The revised documentary rationale does not turn a name, an identifier or local register approval into evidence of an actual mandate.
concepts.review_method: Assistant-supported selected-source comparison, ancestry/neighbor/set-policy review and bounded static identity/dependency checks; no instance-level or independent expert evaluation.

concepts.title: Responsibility Assignment Information
concepts.authored_definition: A recorded statement about an assignment of responsibility or authority, distinct from the relationship it asserts.
concepts.rationale: Retain the claim/relationship contrast. A recorded responsibility assignment can describe an unsupported claim; a provenance association does not supply the full Riskium mandate-grounding contract.
concepts.context_interpretation: R-55 links the statement to at most one actual mandate and allows none. R-09 concerns an analytical RiskCase; neither this statement nor missing approval determines that case's existence. A named owner alone does not establish responsibility, accountability and approval authority together.
concepts.review_method: Assistant-supported selected-source comparison, ancestry/neighbor/set-policy review and bounded static identity/dependency checks; no instance-level or independent expert evaluation.

concepts.title: Responsible Agent Role
concepts.authored_definition: A context-dependent role borne by an agent with an assigned responsibility.
concepts.rationale: Retain an analogy to provenance role/association descriptions. ResponsibleAgentRole is a contextual bearer classification, not a PROV Role function description or the statement recording an assignment.
concepts.context_interpretation: The abstract roleMixin inherits no single sortal identity; its person and organization specializations retain their different identities. R-56 supplies a mandatory inherited mediation dependency. This source structure does not prove that a particular mandate actually exists.
concepts.review_method: Assistant-supported selected-source comparison, ancestry/neighbor/set-policy review and bounded static identity/dependency checks; no instance-level or independent expert evaluation.

concepts.title: Authorizing Agent Role
concepts.authored_definition: A context-dependent role borne by an agent authorized to approve or issue a specified decision or assignment.
concepts.rationale: Retain the bounded analogy. An authorizing role requires a supported authority context; a provenance function or activity participation alone does not establish approval authority.
concepts.context_interpretation: The abstract roleMixin aggregates person and organization bearers without supplying identity. R-57 supplies the selected mandatory dependency. Responsible and authorizing participation are not globally exclusive merely because they share Agent as a parent.
concepts.review_method: Assistant-supported selected-source comparison, ancestry/neighbor/set-policy review and bounded static identity/dependency checks; no instance-level or independent expert evaluation.

concepts.title: Responsible Person
concepts.authored_definition: A person bearing a responsible-agent role in a specified assignment context.
concepts.rationale: Retain the person/function analogy while preserving the assigned responsible-person role as a contextual participation of the same human bearer.
concepts.context_interpretation: G-24 provides the sole inherited identity supplier Person; G-25 supplies the ResponsibleAgentRole path and inherited R-56 mediation. The same human can bear different roles across contexts without being duplicated or merged with an organization.
concepts.review_method: Assistant-supported selected-source comparison, ancestry/neighbor/set-policy review and bounded static identity/dependency checks; no instance-level or independent expert evaluation.

concepts.title: Responsible Organization
concepts.authored_definition: An organization bearing a responsible-agent role in a specified assignment context.
concepts.rationale: Retain the organization/function analogy without substituting a vocabulary function for a supported responsible-organization participation.
concepts.context_interpretation: G-26 preserves the sole Organization identity and G-27 supplies the responsible-role path and inherited R-56 mediation. A corporate representative is not the organization; an organizational record alone is not evidence of a grounded mandate.
concepts.review_method: Assistant-supported selected-source comparison, ancestry/neighbor/set-policy review and bounded static identity/dependency checks; no instance-level or independent expert evaluation.

concepts.title: Authorizing Person
concepts.authored_definition: A person bearing an authorizing-agent role in a specified context.
concepts.rationale: Retain the analogy while separating human identity from supported approval authority. A provenance role label supplies neither a mandate nor a decision-specific authorization policy.
concepts.context_interpretation: G-28 preserves Person identity, G-29 supplies the authorizing-role path and R-57 is inherited. The non-disjoint Person sibling policy permits different contextual roles without asserting that one person fills both distinct participants of one mandate.
concepts.review_method: Assistant-supported selected-source comparison, ancestry/neighbor/set-policy review and bounded static identity/dependency checks; no instance-level or independent expert evaluation.

concepts.title: Authorizing Organization
concepts.authored_definition: An organization bearing an authorizing-agent role in a specified context.
concepts.rationale: Retain the organization/function analogy while treating approval authority as contextual and supported rather than entailed by an organizational name or class membership.
concepts.context_interpretation: G-30 preserves Organization identity; G-31 supplies the authorizing-role path and inherited R-57 dependency. Organizational bearer kinds remain distinct from human representatives, while responsible/authorizing participation is not made globally exclusive.
concepts.review_method: Assistant-supported selected-source comparison, ancestry/neighbor/set-policy review and bounded static identity/dependency checks; no instance-level or independent expert evaluation.

concepts.title: Responsibility Role Term
concepts.authored_definition: A controlled value identifying the kind of responsibility or authority assigned. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.
concepts.rationale: Retain vocabulary-concept/function context. The controlled term denotes a responsibility or authority kind; selecting the term does not instantiate the actual role or the mandate grounding it.
concepts.context_interpretation: The path through ClassificationTerm and VocabularyConcept preserves InformationArtifact identity. R-54 records an assignment's selected term and R-59 a mandate's term; lexical equality alone establishes neither mandate identity nor actual authorization.
concepts.review_method: Assistant-supported selected-source comparison, ancestry/neighbor/set-policy review and bounded static identity/dependency checks; no instance-level or independent expert evaluation.

boundaries.static_scope: Only declared identity-provider, abstractness, inherited mediation and optional resolution/mandate source contracts were checked; not actual individuals, full semantic acceptance or organizational effectiveness.
boundaries.semantic_review: Independent semantic review remains #23; exact normative adoption remains #78.
boundaries.deployment_scope: Previews remain planning artifacts; full component qualification and affected-body publication/readback remain separate.

batch_findings: All ten authored definitions and local edge records are unchanged. Seven concepts have changed ancestor typing context; ResponsibilityAssignmentInformation also has the revised RiskCase as an association neighbor. Direct generalization endpoints are additionally checked so changes to Person/Organization are visible even at the Agent category.

The four concrete person/organization roles each retain exactly one declared ancestor identity provider and inherit their selected mandatory mediation. Agent and the two roleMixins remain abstract non-sortals; their currently modeled descendant bearer identities are Person and Organization. These are selected static source checks, not ontology-engine executions or evidence that a particular mandate is realized.

The disjoint, incomplete AgentKinds set distinguishes bearer kinds. This differs from global exclusion between responsible and authorizing participation, which is not imposed by the blanket mixed-criterion set. Carried role-subtype criteria retain their source statuses and are not independently reapproved here.

ActorReference may remain unresolved under R-53 (0..1), and the assignment statement may lack an actual mandate under R-55 (0..1). An owner name, a PROV function or a controlled responsibility term alone establishes none of the actual relationship, authorization and accountability commitments.
context_guard_note: Bearer-kind exclusivity is separate from contextual participation. Shared parenthood does not create a blanket role set; different contextual roles do not create a new bearer identity. A responsibility statement or provenance function alone does not establish actual authorization, and local operational admission does not determine analytical RiskCase existence.
